title: Action Space Compression Attack: Does Reducing Agent Action Diversity Help Monitoring?
original_idea: Implement action space constraint in ControlArena limiting available tool calls. Measure whether malicious agents can still complete sabotage within constrained space, and whether anomaly detection monitors perform better on constrained vs unconstrained spaces. Vary constraint severity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory connecting capability restriction to monitoring effectiveness, but the outcome is uncertain -- restriction could help monitoring or just displace misbehavior. The safety insight depends on which outcome obtains.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires modifying ControlArena tool configurations and running multiple experimental conditions. Setting up anomaly detection monitors on top of that adds complexity. Feasible in 30hrs but needs ControlArena familiarity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple experimental conditions (varying constraint severity) with two measurements each (sabotage success + monitor performance) creates a reasonably large experiment matrix. Moderately scoped.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
